name: round-2
note: Second round, on a new baseline. Round one (tempo-on-off) ended with one change that held up on the ladder: holding the frostburst for the opening against bots rated 2250 and up (+15 points at 2.1 standard errors there, -11 under 2250). The scouts' default playbook becomes that rating-based playbook (field-marshal/playbooks/default.json written by tools/flagship-playbook.py --out, same as the flagship's), and control is that default. The three arms are questions round one left open because their games were played before the connection fix or were cut short: frost-escape (dash out of a burst thrown at us; +5 points after 51 games), no-tempo (is the tempo evaluation at the leaves worth having; 13 clean games), plan-8 (eight ticks of our own lines against an opponent model; no clean games). Each arm is laid over the per-opponent default, so it changes one thing against every opponent. Every opponent, balanced by opponent, map and seat. Read each arm against control and the plain default games over the same hours, by opponent rating band. Added 12:50Z in the slot plan-8 left: move-prior, the learned movement prior (a model of how the strong bots move, fitted on 922 replay games; it predicts 50% of their moves in unseen games against 43% for a plain table, and on StuartSutcliffe's decisions lifts our movement agreement from 72.6% to 75.4%). Predicts: beats control, most against strong bots. Needs a release at or after 5636346. Added 13:35Z: learned, the movement prior together with the learned attack prior (models of when the strong bots fire, throw the frostburst and use the repulsor; frostburst timing predicted 89% of the time on unseen games, shots 76%). On StuartSutcliffe's decisions the pair lifts attack agreement from 49.3% to 82.6% and movement agreement to 74.6%. Predicts: at least as good as move-prior. Needs a release that has attack_prior_weight. Added 14:25Z: pad-fight. From today's replays of our own games against the top group (20 games, all lost): they take 1.75 power pads a game and we 0.40; in 9 of the 20 games they took a pad after we had stood at least four ticks within 3 tiles of it, no farther from it than they were, without a buff. A power pad is damage x3/2 for 50 ticks. The arm leaves for a pad in time, earns 15 for ending a turn on a power pad that is there, and gives a pad up only when the opponent is all but on it. Predicts: beats control against bots rated 2250 and up, with our power pads there rising from 0.4 toward 1 a game; no change against weaker bots, where we already get the pads. Needs a release that has pad_bonus (7dea220 or later). Added 14:45Z: tree. The new brain: with the opponent in view the turn comes from a tree search for both sides on the exact engine (victris_engine::mcts) run for 250 ms, with none of the hand-set terms of the policy. Offline, against the current search in the arena: 39% at 30 ms a move (18 games), 56% at 150 ms (18 games), 67% at 300 ms (30 games on fresh seeds). This arm is the ladder's confirmation of that offline result. It thinks about 250 ms on every tick with the opponent in view (server charge about 360 ms a tick), by design. Needs a release at or after the commit that adds tree_ms and forcing_depth.
